pages.title: About us
pages.content:
About Kyugo Training

About us

We train the people who are already there when something happens at work.

Kyugo Training was founded in 2011 by Ines Varga after twelve years as an ambulance paramedic. The centre is a 220 m² ground-floor hall in a former ship-chandler’s warehouse at Werfstraat 41, 3511 Utrecht, with a mock warehouse aisle, a mock kitchen and a mock office for scenarios.

Our courses are built on physical repetition and practical competence rather than classroom slide decks. The first minutes before an ambulance arrives depend on what ordinary people on site can actually do, so most of every day is spent kneeling on a mat with a mannequin, an AED trainer and an instructor who corrects the small things.

How we work

  • At most 12 trainees on a course and 6 trainees per instructor in scenarios.
  • Five of the seven hours of a course day are hands-on.
  • The syllabus is reviewed every January against current published resuscitation guidelines.

Fees are in euros per person, excluding 21% VAT. We make no promises about outcomes: a certificate records what you practised and were assessed on, nothing more.

pages.title: Courses & fees
pages.content:
Courses

Courses & fees

Workplace first-aid qualifications built around practice.

Open courses run at our Utrecht centre; closed training days are tailored for company teams and can be held on your own site.

All fees exclude 21% VAT. Training days run 08:30–16:30 with lunch from 12:30 to 13:15. A course takes at most twelve trainees.

Book a group day or write to hello@kyugotraining.example for open dates.

pages.title: A training day
pages.content:
How a day runs

A training day

Drill first, scenario after lunch, assessment before you go home.

Wear clothes you can kneel in and flat shoes. Lunch is a 45-minute break; hot drinks are provided.

pages.title: The certificate
pages.content:
Certificate

The certificate

What the certificate covers, and when it needs renewing.

At the end of the assessment each trainee who has completed the practical stations receives a certificate the same day, and a copy is entered on the employer’s register.

  • Certificates are valid for 3 years.
  • We send a reminder 90 days before expiry.
  • Requalification takes 2 days (14 h) and costs €285; the Annual Refresher is a half day at €75.

The certificate is a record of training completed at Kyugo Training. It does not replace any national or sector requirement; check what applies to your workplace.

pages.title: Instructors
pages.content:
Who teaches

Instructors

Paramedics, safety officers and a scenario builder: people who have done it for real.

  • Ines Varga, founder and lead instructor
  • Tomas Reyes, senior instructor, industrial sites
  • Mirela Haddad, CPR & AED
  • Daniel Mensah, burns & chemical splash
  • Pieter Aalders, scenario coordinator
  • Lucía Ferrer, assessment & certificates
  • Hana Kowalczyk, group bookings

Lead instructor Ines Varga spent twelve years on front-line ambulances before founding Kyugo in 2011 to teach practical workplace readiness. Senior instructor Tomas Reyes coordinates on-site training for manufacturing and logistics facilities.

pages.title: Stories
pages.content:
From our groups

Stories

Real workplaces, ordinary shifts, one practical day.

The firms below are fictional; their stories show how a day is set up around a real floor.

Halvorsen Logistics, Waalhaven

Eighteen night-shift pickers and team leads took Emergency First Aid at Work, with two on-site days of nine.

De Vries Print & Pack

Ten press operators took First Aid at Work plus the Burns & Chemical Splash module.

Marlow House offices

Twenty-four front-desk and security staff took CPR & AED Operator in two half-days of twelve.

Hotel Meridiaan kitchen

Twelve cooks and porters trained in the mock kitchen on burns and chemical splashes.

pages.title: FAQ
pages.content:
Questions

FAQ

Short answers before you book.

How many people are on a course?

At most twelve, with six trainees per instructor in scenarios.

Do we need any prior knowledge?

No. Courses start from the first minute and build up.

How long is a certificate valid?

Three years. We send a reminder 90 days before expiry.

Can you come to our site?

Yes. The on-site group day is €1,480 per group of up to twelve, kit included, booked at least three weeks ahead.

pages.title: Contact & access
pages.content:
Contact

Contact & access

Phone +31 30 555 0142 · hello@kyugotraining.example

Office hours Mon–Fri 08:00–17:30. Training days 08:30–16:30 (lunch 12:30–13:15). Closed weekends and Dutch public holidays.

This is a fictional centre; the address, telephone number and e-mail are samples.

pages.title: Book a group
pages.content:
Book a group

Book a group

From enquiry to certificate in four steps.

  • 1 Enquire. Contact us by form, phone or email; we reply within two working days.
  • 2 Planning call. A 30-minute call on your site, shift patterns, typical risks and the right course.
  • 3 Training day. At your premises or our centre, with dates fixed at least three weeks ahead.
  • 4 Certificates. Issued the same day with an employer register; renewals tracked ninety days before expiry.

On-site group day, up to 12 trainees: €1,480 (excl. VAT, kit included). Write to hello@kyugotraining.example to request a date.

pages.title: Newsletter
pages.content:
Newsletter

Newsletter

Course dates and workplace notes, a few times a year.

We send open course dates for the coming quarter and the occasional note for employers. To join, write to hello@kyugotraining.example with the word “newsletter”; we keep your address only for this list.

posts.title: Open course dates for November
posts.excerpt: Open courses at the Utrecht centre are bookable for individual places every Tuesday in November.
posts.content:
Emergency First Aid at Work runs every Tuesday at the centre on Werfstraat, 08:30 to 16:30, with lunch from 12:30 to 13:15. The fee is €145 per person excl. VAT, and a course takes at most twelve trainees.

The three-day First Aid at Work course runs Monday to Wednesday in the first and third week of the month at €395. CPR & AED Operator is a half day on the second and fourth Thursday, 13:00–16:30, at €85.

Certificates are issued the same day and are valid for three years. Group bookings are handled separately; write to hello@kyugotraining.example.

posts.title: What’s new in this year’s Annual Refresher
posts.excerpt: The refresher syllabus was reviewed in January against current published resuscitation guidelines.
posts.content:
Every January we read the current published resuscitation guidelines against our syllabus and change what needs changing. This year the refresher spends more of its three hours on compression rhythm and AED pad placement and less on lecture.

The Annual Refresher runs on the second and fourth Thursday, 08:30–11:30, for €75 per person excl. VAT. Bring your previous certificate; we send a reminder ninety days before it expires.

posts.title: Planning first-aid cover for night shifts
posts.excerpt: A short guide for employers who run rotating or overnight teams.
posts.content:
A day course on Tuesday does not help a team that works nights. For industrial employers we run closed group days at your premises, up to twelve trainees at €1,480 per group, with the kit and mannequins included.

Book at least three weeks ahead. After a 30-minute planning call about your shift patterns and typical risks, we fix the dates and send the register to the employer on the training day.

posts.title: Where to put an AED on a warehouse floor
posts.excerpt: Three questions we ask on every site visit before a group day.
posts.content:
Can a colleague reach it from the far end of the aisle in under a minute? Is it on a route a person would run without thinking? Can everyone on the shift say where it is?

During a scenario in the mock aisle we time the walk, the call and the handover to the ambulance crew. The answers are usually simpler than the equipment.

posts.title: Our new scenario room: the mock kitchen
posts.excerpt: The hall now has a mock kitchen next to the warehouse aisle and the mock office.
posts.content:
Burns and chemical splashes happen in kitchens, so our 220 m² hall now has a full mock kitchen with a steel counter, a hob and a sink. Pieter Aalders builds the incidents and plays the casualty.

The kitchen is used in the Burns & Chemical Splash module, a half day on the last Friday of the month, 08:30–12:00, for €95 per person excl. VAT.

posts.title: How to prepare staff for their first course day
posts.excerpt: Plain advice for the people you are sending to us.
posts.content:
Wear clothes you can kneel in and flat shoes. You will spend five of the seven hours on the floor, so comfortable matters more than smart.

Bring a lunch or use the break from 12:30 to 13:15. You do not need to revise: the day starts with hands, not slides, and the assessment is a practical check plus ten short written questions.
